newsitem.title: USA: Texas HRW wheat said to be high quality so far.
newsitem.headline: Texas HRW wheat said to be high quality so far.

text.p: Initial samples of new-crop hard red winter wheat from the Texas harvest have displayed high quality characteristics, millers and grain merchandisers said Wednesday.
Millers said that despite having high moisture content, initial loads of new crop wheat appeared to contain large kernels and high test weights.
"As far as test weight and grinding goes, it's looking good so far," said Mark Alfonso, milling superintendent at The Morrison Milling Co in Denton, Texas.
"The texture of the wheat is plump. They're big kernels," Alfonso said. "The last time I've seen this size wheat was about four years ago."
Alfonso said his mill had taken in 40 truckloads of new crop since last week and started grinding some of it Tuesday night. "It performed real well in terms of grinding," he said.
Alfonso said a spot load that arrived from Abilene, Texas, contained a high protein content of around 15 percent and an average test weight of about 62 lbs.
He said he had not yet seen high dockage or evidence of sprout damage, but he cautioned that it was still early.
Alfonso noted that many wheat fields were still "green," or immature, because of the cool, wet spring, and he said it could be some time before this wheat is harvested.

The late spring has caused high moisture levels in Texas wheat, and Alfonso said he had rejected some loads with moisture contents of between 14.5 and 15 percent. He also said producers were actively using dryers to remove moisture from the new crop.
Meanwhile, an Oklahoma grain dealer said his firm had taken in 45 truckloads of new crop wheat earlier this week from around the Fort Worth, Texas area.
"It's probably the best quality stuff we've seen out of Texas in the last five years," the Oklahoma dealer said. "Test weights were good. It's just good, heavy number one or two (grade) wheat."
Another dealer in Kansas said that although protein levels were erratic on one group of Texas samples he had seen, the test weights were high.
"Protein ranged from 10 (percent) all the way up to 17.3. But test weights were pretty strong at 58.8 to 63.5 (pounds)," the dealer said.
